claims.claim: A trained neural network can be distilled into a soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from training data.
claims.quote: We describe a way of using a trained neural net to create a type of soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from the training data.

claims.claim: Rules extracted from neural networks preserve high predictive accuracy of the original networks and are comparable to decision trees in accuracy, number of rules, and conditions per rule.
claims.quote: Experiments demonstrate that rules extracted from neural networks are comparable with those of decision trees in terms of predictive accuracy, number of rules and average number of conditions for a rule; they preserve high predictive accuracy of original networks.

claims.claim: Rule extraction from fuzzy ARTMAP proceeds in two stages: pruning excessive categories and weights, then quantizing continuous weights into descriptive rules.
claims.quote: Rule extraction proceeds in two stages: pruning, which simplifies the network structure by removing excessive recognition categories and weights; and quantization of continuous learned weights, which allows the final system state to be translated into a usable set of descriptive rules.

claims.claim: ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact comprehensible rules whose accuracy and complexity compare favorably to alternative rule extraction algorithms.
claims.quote: Simulation results consistently indicate that ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact sets of comprehensible rules for which accuracy and complexity compare favorably to rules extracted by alternative algorithms.

claims.claim: A review categorizes rule extraction algorithms into decompositional, pedagogical, and eclectic schemes and evaluates them by target neural network structure.
claims.quote: This paper has thoroughly reviewed various rule extraction algorithms, considering the classification scheme: decompositional, pedagogical, and eclectics. It also presents the evaluation of these algorithms based on the neural network structure with which the algorithm is intended to work.

claims.claim: The review finds limited study of rule extraction algorithms for deep neural networks.
claims.quote: The main contribution of this review is to show that there is a limited study of rule extraction algorithm from DNN.

claims.claim: Knowledge distillation formulates neural network compression into decision trees as multi-output regression, achieving 1% to 5% better accuracy than vanilla decision trees at the same depth.
claims.quote: We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1% to 5%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth.

claims.claim: This work claims to be the first to distill deep neural networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.
claims.quote: To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

claims.claim: Any neural network with any activation function can be exactly represented as a decision tree with no loss of accuracy.
claims.quote: In this manuscript, we show that any neural network with any activation function can be represented as a decision tree. The representation is equivalence and not an approximation, thus keeping the accuracy of the neural network exactly as is.

claims.claim: The exact decision tree equivalence holds for fully connected and convolutional networks with skip connections and normalizations.
claims.quote: The analysis holds both for fully connected and convolutional networks, which may or may not also include skip connections and/or normalizations.

claims.claim: The dsmtree distillation method transfers hierarchical decision logic into neural networks matching teacher performance within 2% on many benchmarks.
claims.quote: dsmtree, a novel distillation method that transfers hierarchical decision logic into neural networks, matching teacher performance within 2% on many benchmarks.

open_questions: How do distillation methods compare quantitatively across architectures (CNNs, transformers, etc.) and tasks beyond classification?
What are the computational trade-offs (inference speed, model size) of the extracted rules/trees versus original networks?
How well do these methods scale to large modern networks (millions of parameters) and high-dimensional inputs?
What fidelity metrics beyond accuracy (e.g., calibration, robustness, out-of-distribution behavior) are preserved?
Are there theoretical guarantees on approximation quality for the pedagogical and decompositional approaches?
